content: 1. The interaction between levonorgestrel intrauterine systems and antithrombin alfa may result in pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially reducing the efficacy of either agent. This combination should be avoided or alternative therapies considered due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 2. Levonorgestrel intrauterine systems and antithrombin III may also exhibit pharmacodynamic antagonism, leading to decreased effects of either agent. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies to mitigate the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 3. Apalutamide can decrease the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 4. The combination of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems and argatroban may result in pharmacodynamic antagonism, reducing the efficacy of either agent. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 5. Bemiparin and levonorgestrel intrauterine systems may interact through pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially reducing the effects of either agent. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies to address the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 6. Bivalirudin and levonorgestrel intrauterine systems may also exhibit pharmacodynamic antagonism, leading to decreased efficacy of either agent. Avoid this combination or use alternative therapies due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 7. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 10. Levonorgestrel intrauterine systems may reduce the efficacy of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogen-containing contraceptives are expected to reduce elagolix efficacy, while the effects of progestin-only contraceptives on elagolix are unknown. Advise women to use nonhormonal contraceptives during elagolix treatment and for one week after discontinuation. 11. Encorafenib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. Hormonal contraceptives may lose efficacy when coadministered with encorafenib. Women of childbearing potential should use highly effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for two weeks after the final dose. 12. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 13. Lesinurad decreases the effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid relying solely on hormonal contraception when taking lesinurad. Use additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 17. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. 18. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during coadministration. 19. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine systems by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Advise patients to use contraception methods unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction or add nonhormonal contraception during coadministration and for four months after the last dose. 20.
